spec.description: A Ripple spec is a JSON object with two top-level fields that matter for rendering: `ui` (the node tree the renderer mounts — REQUIRED) and `state` (the StateManager seed — required when any node uses `bind` or reads `{state.*}`). The renderable tree field is named `ui` exactly — never `root`, `tree`, `view`, `body`, or `content`. Specs that use those aliases will not render.

set.description: Assign `value` to the state path `target`. The most common action — use it to update any state field.

shape.value?: any — value to assign. Supports {state.x} expressions.

toggle.description: Flip a boolean target, or toggle membership of `value` in an array target.

shape.target: string — state path. If boolean, value is inverted; if array, `value` is added or removed.
shape.value?: any — when target is an array, the membership toggle key.

push.description: Append `value` to the array at `target`. Creates the array if undefined.

shape.target: string — state path to an array.

remove.description: Remove an item from the array at `target` — by `value` (equality match) or by `index`.

shape.target: string — state path to an array.
shape.value?: any — first matching item is removed.

open.description: Set the target state path to `true`. Idiomatic shortcut for opening a modal or dialog whose `value` is bound to that path.

shape.target: string — state path that controls the modal/dialog open state.

navigate.description: Host-delegated URL change. The host's `onEvent` callback performs the navigation.

toast.description: Show a toast notification. Use after `set` / `api` to give the user feedback.

emit.description: Emit a custom event up to the host. Use to hand control back to the host pipeline (e.g. "submit complete, take it from here").

pin.description: Host-delegated bookmark/pin operation. The host implements the persistence.

shape.value?: any — payload describing the pinned item.

api.description: Host-delegated HTTP call. The host performs the request; the response is written to `response_key` (if given) and `on_success` runs. On failure `on_error` runs and the error is exposed at state path `_flow_error`.

shape.body?: object — request body. Values support {state.x} expressions.
shape.response_key?: string — state path to write the response into.
shape.on_success?: EventHandler[] — runs after a successful response.

run_source.description: Re-run a server-side read binding ("source") by name. The host re-fetches the source; on success `on_success` runs with the fresh data, on failure `on_error` runs and the error is exposed at state path `_flow_error`. Use it to refresh a data-backed widget after a mutation.

shape.source: string — name of the server-side source to re-run.
shape.on_success?: EventHandler[] — runs with the refreshed data after a successful re-run.

call_binding.description: Invoke a named server-side write binding. The host performs the write; `path` / `params` support {state.x} expressions, resolved before the call. On success `on_success` runs with the result; on failure `on_error` runs and the error is exposed at state path `_flow_error`. The HTTP verb lives in the spec — never name it here.

shape.binding: string — name of the server-side write binding to invoke.
shape.path?: string — path segment for the binding. Supports {state.x}/{item.id} interpolation.
shape.params?: object — parameter map for the write. Values support {state.x}/{item.id} expressions.
shape.on_success?: EventHandler[] — runs with the result data after a successful write.

invoke_tool.description: Invoke a named server-side tool (WebFetch / Composio / etc.) with resolved args. The host POSTs to /pockets/{id}/tools/run with the tool name + args; `args` values support {state.x}/{item.id} expressions, resolved before the call. On success `on_success` runs with the result; on failure `on_error` runs and the error is exposed at state path `_flow_error`. Use it on a Refresh button when the data comes from a tool rather than a declared source.

shape.tool: string — id of the server-side tool to invoke (e.g. "WebFetch", "GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS").
shape.args?: object — argument map for the tool. Values support {state.x}/{item.id} expressions.
shape.on_success?: EventHandler[] — runs with the result data after a successful invocation.

flow.description: Run a list of handlers sequentially. If any step throws `FlowAbortError` (e.g. failed `validate`), `on_error` runs.

branch.description: Evaluate `if` and run `then` or `else`. The condition is a Ripple expression string (e.g. "state.count > 5").

shape.if: string — Ripple expression evaluated as boolean.

confirm.description: Show the ConfirmDialog, suspend the flow, and run `on_confirm` or `on_cancel` based on the user's choice.

shape.message: string — body shown in the dialog.

validate.description: If `condition` is falsy, show a toast and abort the enclosing flow (FlowAbortError). Silent on pass.

shape.condition: string — Ripple expression. Falsy aborts the flow.

delay.description: Pause the flow for the given number of milliseconds. Useful for optimistic-UI demos and animations.

invoke.description: Call a registered widget method by widget id. Used for imperative actions on widgets that expose them (e.g. focusing an input).

animate.description: Imperatively trigger a motion on a target node by id (host-delegated). Use sparingly — most animation belongs in the node-level `motion` field, not an action.

shape.target: string — id of the node to animate.
shape.motion: object — a motion directive (see the motion field schema), e.g. { tap: { scale: 0.96 } }.

motion.description: Add a `motion` field to ANY node (sibling to props/class/style, never inside props) to animate it. Vocabulary: enter/exit, hover/tap/focus, inView (reveal on scroll), scroll (parallax), stagger, and transition (use a semantic preset — never raw numbers). MotionState channels are GPU-safe only (opacity, x, y, scale, rotate, blur). transition.delay is in SECONDS (e.g. 0.12 = 120ms); cascade a row by giving each child delay = index * 0.12. Reduced-motion and SSR are handled by the runtime — do not add them.
motion.budgetRule: MOTION BUDGET: animate entrances and the PRIMARY call-to-action only. Leave everything else at rest. Default transition is `snappy`. Over-animating reads as cheap — restraint reads as premium.

presets.snappy: spring, lively but controlled — the default for entrances and CTAs.
presets.bouncy: spring with overshoot — playful accents, use rarely.

streaming.description: Agent is still reasoning — collapsed, the summary names the last thinking step, else "Reasoning…".

widgets.description: Human-in-the-loop approval card: shows a proposed agent action with a risk badge, an optional diff and tool-call list, and Approve/Deny/Edit controls that resolve and persist the decision.

title.description: The proposed action, e.g. "Update 3 customer records".

summary.description: Optional one-line summary under the title.

risk.description: Risk level: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'. Drives the badge + tone.

decision.description: Decision state: 'pending' | 'approved' | 'denied'. Bind to persist it.

actionId.description: Identifier for the proposed action, passed back to the host callbacks.

diff.description: Before/after payload ({ before, after, mode, layout, title }) rendered with the Diff widget.

toolCalls.description: Proposed tool calls — each rendered with the ToolCall widget.

body.description: Markdown body shown alongside the structured parts.

decidedBy.description: Who decided — shown in the resolved stamp ("Approved by Ada").

disabled.description: Disable the controls (e.g. while the host persists the decision).

askDenyReason.description: Deny first asks for an optional reason, passed to the host as ondeny({ actionId, reason }). Default false.
